# Input drift report (row 11.5.2)

**Generated by:** `python -m terser.monitoring.input_drift` (`src/terser/monitoring/input_drift.py`),
CPU only. Reference window = train split (4,955 prompts). Per-run artifacts (Evidently HTML,
Evidently JSON snapshot, summary JSON, summary markdown) are in `reports/monitoring/`.

> **Note (2026-10-18).** The detector changed after these runs: PSI now uses 3-10 bins sized to
> the smaller window, and each feature's threshold is 0.2 plus its expected PSI under no drift.
> `mmd_samples` is now reported per side. The numbers below predate that change. Windows of 200+
> prompts keep 10 bins, so their PSI values are unchanged; only the thresholds rise slightly.

## Method

| View | Feature(s) | Statistic |
|---|---|---|
| Embedding | bge-small 384-d prompt embeddings (row 6.1) projected on a 16-component PCA fitted to the reference (36.0% of embedding variance) | PSI per component (10 reference-quantile bins, proportions floored at 1e-4); unbiased MMD² with an RBF kernel (median-heuristic bandwidth) on the 16 components, permutation p-value (500 permutations, ≤ 500 rows per side) |
| Length | prompt length in whitespace words | PSI (same binning) |
| Category | task category (`category` field; rows without one get the real-slice rule tag, else `unknown`) | categorical PSI |
| Evidently | the same 18 columns (16 PCs, `length_words`, `category`) | `DataDriftPreset(method="psi", threshold=0.2)`, Evidently 0.7.23 |

**Alert rule:** PSI > 0.2 on any of the 18 features, or MMD permutation p < 0.01. An alert logs a
`CRITICAL` record on `terser.alerts`, the CLI exits 1 (0 otherwise), and the summary JSON carries
`"alert": true` plus the list of reasons; the last stdout line is a JSON verdict with artifact paths,
for the scheduled `drift_flow`.

Embeddings: train prompts come from the row 6.1 cache (`data/processed/embeddings/train_bge_small`);
val and real-slice prompts are not in it, so they were embedded once with the same
`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` on CPU (≈ 40 s for 1,133 prompts) and stored in a text-hash keyed cache
(`data/interim/drift_embeddings/drift_bge_small`, git-ignored). Later runs reuse it (`--no-encode`
runs take ≈ 5 s).

## Results

| Run | Current window | n current | Verdict | Exit | Max PSI (feature) | MMD² | MMD p | Evidently drifted columns |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | val split (`data/processed/splits/val.jsonl`) | 1,133 | **no drift** | 0 | 0.042 (category) | 0.00025 | 0.220 | 0 / 18 |
| B | val split, `code` only (`--current-category code`) | 220 | **DRIFT** | 1 | 7.315 (category) | 0.27024 | 0.002 | 17 / 18 |
| C | real-prompt slice (row 2.1.8, `data/processed/real_slice/test.jsonl`) | 1,000 | **DRIFT** | 1 | 1.167 (pc_1) | 0.04687 | 0.002 | 11 / 18 |

- **A (expected: no drift).** Every PSI is ≤ 0.042 (largest PC: pc_14 at 0.042; length 0.009);
  MMD p = 0.22. The largest value is the category mix. The split is grouped by source prompt, so
  val has fewer `explain` prompts (10.8% vs 16.3%) and more `fact` prompts (20.7% vs 15.7%), which is
  still well under the 0.2 threshold. Evidently flags nothing either.
- **B (deliberate category shift).** A single-category window is flagged on every view: category
  PSI 7.3, 13 of 16 PCs above 0.2 (pc_1 6.85), length PSI 0.46 (code prompts have a narrower length
  range, p90 112 vs 172 words), MMD p at its 1/501 floor.
- **C (real traffic vs synthetic casualised prompts).** The category mix is not flagged (PSI 0.004).
  The slice was balanced by category when it was built. What is flagged is length (PSI 0.70; median
  29 vs 62 words) and the embedding (7 PCs above 0.2, pc_1 1.17, MMD p at floor). This is the
  synthetic-vs-real gap that row 2.1.8 guards against. Live traffic that looks like the real slice
  would raise this alert every day.

Evidently's PSI values agree with ours to within its different binning (e.g. A pc_1 0.035 vs
0.035, C length 0.714 vs 0.698, B category 7.315 vs 7.315); the alert decision uses our values.

The HTML links above work only after `dvc pull`: the files are tracked with DVC (`reports/monitoring/*.html.dvc`) and are not in git. Each Evidently HTML file is about 4.8 MB, almost all of it Evidently's inlined JS bundle; the data
itself is about 5 KB (see the JSON snapshot). The CLI deletes the HTML and keeps only the JSON
when a file goes over 5 MB.

## Reproduce

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m terser.monitoring.input_drift --name train_vs_val
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m terser.monitoring.input_drift --current-category code --name train_vs_val_code
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m terser.monitoring.input_drift \
    --current data/processed/real_slice/test.jsonl --name train_vs_real_slice
# daily, on a serving request log:
python -m terser.monitoring.input_drift --current logs/requests.jsonl --name "$(date +%F)"
```

Synthetic-shift sanity checks: `tests/monitoring/test_input_drift.py`. Same-distribution data is not
flagged. An embedding mean shift, longer prompts and a skewed category mix are each flagged, and
only on their own feature. The CLI exit code and the `CRITICAL` record are also tested.

## Caveats

- **Request logs are hashed by default (row 11.5.6).** Records without `consent_raw_text` have no
  prompt to embed or measure, so the CLI skips them and reports how many it skipped. Daily drift on
  live traffic only covers consented requests. If consent is rare, that is a biased sample.
- **MMD p has a floor.** With 500 permutations the smallest possible p is 1/501 ≈ 0.002. Runs B and
  C both hit it.
- **PSI on small windows.** Under no drift, PSI is roughly (bins − 1)·(1/n_cur + 1/n_ref): about 0.05
  at n_cur = 200 and about 0.01 at n_cur = 1,000. Windows smaller than about 100 prompts start to
  approach the 0.2 threshold by chance. The code requires at least 20 rows per window; a daily job
  on low traffic should pool days.
- Real-slice categories are rule-tagged (`category_source: "rules"`), not judged.
- The 16 components cover 36% of embedding variance. Neither PSI nor MMD (which also runs on the 16
  components) can see a shift confined to the other 64%. Raise `--components` if that matters.
